correctness.rationale: The source linearization contains additive compensated Poisson jumps with amplitude h_i=ln(1+eta_i). For a Hurwitz drift matrix, the stationary Lévy convolution has fourth cumulant equal to the integral of the fourth power of the propagated jump amplitude. The explicit one-atom witness has a nonzero susceptible jump and a Hurwitz linearization, so the e1 projection has strictly positive fourth cumulant and cannot be Gaussian. The source local Fokker–Planck equation also lacks the nonlocal shift term of the jump generator. The exact second-cumulant rate ln(1.1)^2 differs from the source coefficient 2(0.1-ln(1.1)).

originality.rationale: Non-Gaussian stationary laws for Lévy-driven Ornstein–Uhlenbeck processes are established prior knowledge and are not claimed as new. The original contribution is the source-specific diagnosis and exact admissible witness showing that the SVI paper's Theorem 5.1 and covariance equation cannot be exact for its printed nonzero-jump model. Exact-title, DOI, density, Gaussian, Lévy-generator, correction, and erratum searches found no published source-specific repair.
residual_risks: The proof text uses the word approximately near its Gaussian ansatz even though Theorem 5.1 displays the density as a theorem; if read only as a heuristic approximation, no asymptotic scaling or error bound is supplied.
The full text of the 2005 and 2001 general Lévy-OU references was not required for the source-specific cumulant proof and was not fully inspected here.
A non-indexed author note could acknowledge the density-formula issue.

value.rationale: The density-function calculation is presented as a main analytic contribution of the source and is used to interpret stochastic fluctuations around the quasi-endemic state. Replacing a jump process by a local Gaussian forward equation changes not only higher tails but already the covariance for the explicit admissible witness. The correction cleanly separates the valid Brownian-only Gaussian boundary from genuine jump regimes and identifies the nonlocal equation required for any exact density analysis.
